description: Action Network PRO review, checked 7 Nov 2026: web and app prices, the no refund terms, what the free pick records show, and what users report.
dek: The paid tier of Action Network, a betting media site owned by Better Collective. PRO costs $14.99 a week to $119.99 a year on the web, sells faster pick alerts, projections, money percentages and system picks, and its terms say payments are nonrefundable. The site also earns commissions from sportsbooks.

short_answer: Action Network is a real, large betting media business. It names its company, its New York address and its parent, Better Collective, and it publishes PRO prices and subscription terms. In that sense PRO is legitimate: you pay and you get access to a set of tools.

What PRO does not do is prove its picks win. The PRO page shows no win rate or return, and the only result style wording is a feature called "Historically profitable systems" plus one customer quote. Expert picks themselves are listed as free; PRO adds instant alerts, projections, money percentages, system picks and premium articles. The free picks page shows each expert's last 30 days, which is a short window that swings both ways.

Treat PRO as a data and tools subscription, not a proven winning pick service. If you buy, start with the shortest plan, cancel before it renews if it is not useful, and track any pick you follow yourself with the line and time you got it.

guarantee: There is no guarantee. The terms of use say you may cancel any time, "however, there are no refunds for cancellation," and that there are no refunds or credits for partly used billing periods. After you cancel, access runs to the end of the current billing period. The terms also say Action Network is unable to refund subscriptions bought through iOS or Google Play, so those go through Apple or Google.

The terms say a subscription may begin with a free trial whose length is shown at checkout, that the card is charged when the trial ends unless you cancel first, and that once a charge is made "there is no refund available." Introductory rates renew at the normal rate. The terms page we read says it was last updated on February 8th, 2018, and still refers to "Edge memberships," so parts of it may not match today's plans. Losses on bets you place are never covered.

claims.where: PRO page, quoted App Store review

claims.claim: Calls its app five star rated

claims_note: The about page does not hold one story. It says Action Network was founded in 2017 and also that it was launched in 2018. It claims "18+" years of betting data in one heading and data gathered for "more than 15 years" in the next sentence. On 7 Nov 2026 its app rating field read "(need current figure/source)", which looks like an unfinished draft left on a live page.

Nothing on the PRO page says what "historically profitable" means: which period, which prices, how many plays, and how the systems did after they were published. A betting system found by searching old results will usually look profitable on those same results. Ask for results from after each system went live.
record: The free picks page lists each expert's latest picks with the line, the odds, the units and the game time, plus a last 30 day record in wins, losses and units. On 7 Nov 2026 those records ranged from 77-79-0 (-9.2u) to 403-339-10 (+44.4u). That is more than most pick sellers show, and it includes losing records. But 30 days is a small window, and we did not find a full, time stamped history for the experts or for the PRO system picks on any page we opened.
The PRO page itself shows no record at all. Its feature table lists Expert Picks as free and Instant Expert Pick Alerts as PRO only, so what PRO mainly sells for picks is speed, not access.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Action Network expert or PRO system is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Action Network shows its experts' records over 30 days only. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: There is a lot of feedback on the Action Network app, but very little that is about PRO itself. Most reviews judge the free app, its bet tracker and its news. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: A Covers member who had paid for PRO in 2021 said he used it mainly for public and sharp money data, found the headline picks lost more often than they won, and went back to the free version.
The Apple App Store page showed a rating of 4.8 out of 5 from about 39K ratings. That is a large sample, but it rates the whole app, most of which is free, not the PRO picks.

customers.date: Oct 2 (year not shown on the page)
customers.text: An App Store reviewer who had tracked bets in the app for years said a forced update made manual bet entry slower and hid pending bets. He later added that a newer update fixed many of the issues and raised his rating to 5 stars. The developer replied that most bugs were fixed.

An App Store reviewer said bets synced from BetMGM could still be deleted, so a user's public record could drop losing bets, and described watching one followed bettor's losses disappear. This is about user profiles in the app, not PRO experts, and it is from 2021. We did not check whether it still applies.

On Trustpilot, which showed 8 reviews and a TrustScore of 3.9 for actionnetwork.com, one reviewer who said he was a long time PRO subscriber called the monthly fee good value for frequent bettors. The price he named was lower than today's.

Two 1 star Trustpilot reviews: one said a $70 referral reward had not been paid after two months, and one gave no detail beyond calling the site lies. Most other Trustpilot reviews, from March 2026, praise the free news and casino content, not PRO. Eight reviews is not a sample.
The PRO page quotes one App Store review saying the app "has paid for itself." It was chosen by the seller, so it cannot tell you what a typical buyer experiences.

We found no Reddit thread with a substantial discussion of PRO in our searches, and no Better Business Bureau profile we could confirm belongs to Action Network. Our searches found no regulator action against the company.

conflicts: Action Network's about page says it "generates revenue through subscriptions, partnerships, and affiliate relationships with sportsbooks, online casinos and prediction markets," and that these "may result in commissions when users sign up or place bets through links on the platform." It claims more than 77 sportsbook and DFS partnerships, naming DraftKings, BetMGM, Caesars, Fanatics Sportsbook and PrizePicks.

The site runs bonus code pages for sportsbooks. On 7 Nov 2026 its BetMGM page promoted the code ACTIONGET1 and stated "We may be compensated for the links provided on this page." Affiliate deals often pay more when referred customers bet more. The about page says editorial picks are independent of these deals; we could not test that. Its parent, Better Collective, is a sports betting media group listed in Stockholm and Copenhagen.
strengths: A named company, a New York address, a known parent and published prices and terms.
Expert picks are free and each expert's last 30 days is shown with units, including losing records, so you can watch before paying.
Short plans exist. A weekly plan lets you try PRO for $14.99 instead of committing to a year.
concerns: No refunds. The terms say payments are nonrefundable, trials convert to paid plans and plans auto renew.
No record for PRO system picks or the "historically profitable" systems on any page we opened, and expert records cover 30 days only.
The business earns commissions from sportsbooks when users sign up or bet through its links.
Prices differ between the web and the App Store, and the terms page was last updated in 2018.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A 30 day record is not a track record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the refund and renewal terms before you pay, and put the renewal date in your calendar.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any expert or system a few hundred picks before you call it a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real subscription from a real company, owned by Better Collective, with published prices and terms. We could not verify that its picks or systems win over time, because no full record was shown on the pages we opened.
How much does Action Network PRO cost?
On 7 Nov 2026 the web page showed $14.99 a week, $24.99 a month or $119.99 a year. The App Store page listed other in app prices, from $14.99 for a week to $119.99 for a year.
Does Action Network PRO give refunds?
The terms say no. You can cancel any time and keep access until the end of the billing period, but payments are nonrefundable, and app store purchases go through Apple or Google.
Does Watchdog track Action Network PRO?
Not yet. No Action Network expert or PRO system is matched to a Watchdog graded record in this edition. If that changes, this page will say so and show the record.
